checks.workload: 16 KiB binary identities mixed with multibyte and embedded-NUL text in UTF-8, UTF-16le and UTF-16be databases; 40 KiB read allowance.
checks.invariant: Point reads and iteration preserve storage classes and values without reserving text-conversion space for binary data; smaller allowances still reject and all reservations release.

checks.workload: A 32 KiB BLOB followed by integer and text fields, with an allowance equal to the independently constructed encoded row.
checks.invariant: Exactly one complete output buffer fits the allowance, produces the pinned native bytes and releases all retained memory.

checks.workload: 20 vectors of 4096 dimensions under 256 KiB, retained readers, savepoint and transaction rollback, replacement, tombstone rebuild and cold reopen.
checks.invariant: The original allowance holds every lifecycle operation; retained and reopened queries keep their independently checked results and cleanup releases all memory.

checks.workload: 128/512 one-KiB records adopted into independent 128 KiB and undersized 1 KiB allowances.
checks.invariant: Different allowances copy and charge their own run; insufficient budgets fail, closing the source releases all original leases and the independent root retains exact results.

checks.workload: 512 records through unordered and ordered construction under a 64 KiB ancestor with 32 KiB retained elsewhere and a larger child allowance.
checks.invariant: Resident growth leaves room for disk conversion, preserving exact values, independent roots and complete final allowance release.

checks.workload: 257 indivisible rows with duplicate keys under a one-byte encoded allowance, full drain and early stop.
checks.invariant: One physical file during initial-run construction, the same 257 runs and fixed-fan-in merge passes, exact stable output and complete file cleanup.

checks.workload: Adjacent small and multi-block values in one encrypted file, rejected append to an older segment and retained repeatable readers.
checks.invariant: Readers stay within their own bytes, rejected append preserves file contents and pending ownership, and the final reader releases the sole file.
